market_news.paragraph: Global equities were broadly weaker in the latest completed round of trading, with 7 of the 24 benchmarks tracked on this page closing higher. In the United States, the S&P 500 fell 0.58 per cent to 7,673.52, the Dow Jones fell 1.18 per cent to 52,786, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.32 per cent to 26,421 and the Russell 2000 fell 0.52 per cent to 2,960.20. In Europe, the FTSE 100 fell 0.16 per cent to 10,794, the DAX fell 0.52 per cent to 25,871 and the CAC 40 fell 0.70 per cent to 8,259.50. Across Asia, the Nikkei 225 fell 0.19 per cent to 65,143, the Hang Seng fell 0.27 per cent to 25,248, the KOSPI rose 1.40 per cent to 7,051.64, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.28 per cent to 3,951.51, the BSE Sensex fell 0.57 per cent to 75,146 and the Straits Times fell 0.71 per cent to 5,726.29. Elsewhere, the Ibovespa rose 1.20 per cent to 187,367. Locally, the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.11 per cent to 8,911.40 and the All Ordinaries fell 0.13 per cent to 9,102.90. In digital assets, bitcoin changed hands at $79,235, up 1.02 per cent over the past 24 hours. In currencies, the US dollar bought 1.3861 Australian dollars, little changed against the prior business day's fix. Index levels, exchange rates and commodity prices on this page are captured live at build time from the sources linked in each section; no forward-looking view is offered here.
